records.text:
# Runtime adapter extension API

An explicit adapter can now join the production Iris runtime without editing
Photon or the mixin. `IrisAdapterRuntime.register(descriptor, sources, exports)`
registers its declaration, independently pinned source bindings and exact
operation-to-uniform exports during client startup. Photon remains the sole
supported reference; registering a descriptor does not establish shader support.
The pure [adapter contract](LOD_ADAPTER_CONTRACT.md) and
[source/runtime binding contract](LOD_ADAPTER_BINDING.md) still apply.

## Startup registration

Call the API before Iris starts the first `generalCommonUniforms` registration.
The mixin seals at that method's HEAD, before core/effects/capability suppliers
bind. Its existing tail callbacks also seal when invoked independently. The
production runtime takes one immutable descriptor/source/export/option-key
snapshot and uses it for all subsequent pipelines and shader reloads.
Registration after that boundary throws `IllegalStateException` with an explicit
startup requirement. There is no hot adapter registration or cache invalidation.
An early `IrisAdapterRuntime.snapshot()` returns unavailable without sealing.

For example, client initialization can declare the following operation and
register independently reviewed source bindings:

```java
var operation = new WorkKey(Effect.REFLECTIONS,
        "example:reflection_steps", WorkKind.COUNT);
var descriptor = new AdapterDescriptor(
        new AdapterIdentity("example:reference", "exact-reviewed-revision"),
        List.of(new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:core", Set.of(2)),
                new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:effects", Set.of(2)),
                new ProtocolRequirement("shaderlod:capabilities", Set.of(1))),
        List.of(new WorkCapability(operation, new WorkCapability.CountFloor(1))));
// reviewedSources is a List<SourceBinding> with this exact descriptor identity,
// full container digests, exact consuming member digests and required Iris options.
IrisAdapterRuntime.register(descriptor, reviewedSources,
```

behind. The API rejects:

  explicitly require capabilities 1; no protocol compatibility is inferred.

  operations, and uniform names already assigned to another export.

  underscores, and collisions with existing core/effects/schema fields.

# Shared spatial LOD reconstruction plan

The general mechanism in
[`spatial_plan.glsl`](../shaderpacks/common/shaders/include/shaderlod/spatial_plan.glsl)
turns a validated shared work policy into explicit full, quarter and sixteenth
evaluation tiers with centered reconstruction transitions. It is ShaderLOD code;
no Photon algorithm or upstream attribution was copied or removed. Existing
policy helpers, reference Photon archives/manifests, mod transport and runtime
classes are unchanged by this bounded assignment.

Include `work_policy.glsl` first, then `spatial_plan.glsl`. The public entry point is:

```glsl
ShaderlodSpatialPlan plan = shaderlod_spatial_plan_decide(policy,
    capability_valid, quality_valid, protected_work,
    conservative_region_distance_blocks, supported_rates);
```

`policy` is the existing `ShaderlodWorkPolicy`. All protocol, mode, numeric-domain,
global-enable, inheritance, quality and protection checks delegate to
`shaderlod_work_decide`. Sixteen virtual members with zero minimum reuse that
validation and continuous distance request; their integer work count does not
select a spatial tier. There are no uniforms, samplers, derivatives, projection
assumptions, options, new transport or capability schema.

Distance is radial camera-relative Euclidean distance in Minecraft blocks.
Adapters supply the nearest valid receiver distance across their complete region
and must resolve near/member protection before expensive work. Distance alone is
not a quality certificate. The shared plan does not classify geometry, establish
surface continuity, allocate caches, synchronize passes or perform lighting.

`supported_rates` is a bit mask: bit 1 means full, bit 2 means one evaluation per
2 × 2 region, and bit 4 means one per 4 × 4 region. Full is mandatory. Policy
medium/far endpoints must be exactly 1, 0.25 or 0.0625 and both must be supported.
Other valid ratios, missing endpoint capabilities and requests for skipping retain
full reconstruction at every distance with UNSUPPORTED reason. Invalid masks
retain full with INVALID reason. There is no rounding to the nearest tier, nor
implicit interpolation through an unavailable tier. A caller can deliberately
choose a supported policy before invoking the helper.

| Result | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `weights` | Nonnegative normalized linear reconstruction weights: x full, y quarter, z sixteenth |
| `requested_ratio` | Continuous shared-policy request, retained as diagnostic even when tier support forces full |
| `reconstruction_ratio` | Weight-average legal evaluation fractions; describes reconstruction, not physical cost |
| `evaluation_ratio` | Sum of the fractions of every positive-weight tier, before classification/cache/reconstruction cost |
| `evaluate_full`, `evaluate_medium`, `evaluate_far` | Exactly the positive-weight tiers that must have valid current evaluations |
| `reason` | Existing SHADERLOD_WORK_* reason; POLICY only for a supported eligible plan |

`shaderlod_spatial_plan_full(requested_ratio, reason)` is the full fallback
constructor. Use it with already validated diagnostics. Unknown protocols,
invalid distances/bands/ratios, disabled global/effect state, FULL, unresolved
INHERIT, missing capability, protection or failed quality use weights (1,0,0),
full evaluation and the original shader path. Ordinary shared-policy fallbacks
report unity request. A supported unity policy also collapses to one full
evaluation. The original/mod-absent and disabled baseline therefore needs no
spatial cache or reduced producer work. Call the plan and all guards before
expensive evaluations; blending or branching after full evaluation does not avoid
that work.

## Transitions and evaluation cost

Let m/f be the existing near/far centered smoothstep blends, clamped to [0,1]
to keep endpoint rounding from producing negative weights. The full-policy,
medium-policy and far-policy endpoint contributions are respectively
`(1-m)*(1-f)`, `m*(1-f)` and `f`. Each contribution is added to its exact legal
tier. Equal endpoints collapse into a single evaluation. Existing validation
forbids overlapping transition bands, so at most two distinct tiers are active.
Weights sum to one within binary32 rounding. Zero-width bands switch exactly at
the boundary; touching bands retain the middle endpoint where they meet.

For 32/96/8 blocks and medium/far ratios 0.25/0.0625, near transition endpoints are
28–36 blocks and far endpoints are 92–100 blocks:

| Distance (blocks) | Full / quarter / sixteenth weights | Request | Active tier evaluation ratio |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: |
| 28 | 1 / 0 / 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 32 | 0.5 / 0.5 / 0 | 0.625 | 1.25 |
| 36–92 | 0 / 1 / 0 | 0.25 | 0.25 |
| 96 | 0 / 0.5 / 0.5 | 0.15625 | 0.3125 |
| 100+ | 0 / 0 / 1 | 0.0625 | 0.0625 |

Full plus quarter evaluation in the first transition is more work than full
alone, even before overhead. A full-to-sixteenth blend similarly costs 1.0625.
The continuous request is not a strict physical cap. The adapter must evaluate
each active tier or read a valid current-frame result, then reconstruct the
same declared linear quantity with these weights. Do not multiply lighting
strength, density, radiance or material values by retention. Per-recipient
full-resolution material/albedo composition remains the adapter's responsibility.

Invalid cache entries, invalid receiver regions, resource mismatches and unknown
producer readiness must resolve to original full evaluation. Do not mix through
holes or use stale output across reloads, modes, world changes or resizing. See
[`SURFACE_REGION_CONTINUITY.md`](SURFACE_REGION_CONTINUITY.md) for the separate
all-member surface guard and its lighting-frequency limitations. The shared
pipeline worker owns producer/resolve contracts and actual legal storage.

# Benchmark guide

Use the maintained command for discovery, planning, execution and results:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py discover
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py plan --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py check --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_CHECK_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test --slot SLOT --pack ORIGINAL.zip --pack-options OPTIONS.txt --feature FEATURE --output FRESH_REPORT
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py report --output REPORT
```

`discover` lists local managed slots, worlds and shader archives. It is an inventory, not compatibility approval. Use `--profile` instead of `--slot` for an explicit prepared client. Set `--width` and `--height` to the intended native viewport (the local Asahi fullscreen mode is 2560×1600). Select the exact original pack/options for the feature; private candidates use `--candidate` instead of `--feature`. See the [candidate reference](BENCHMARK_CANDIDATES.md) for specialized scenes, compatibility checks and qualification protocols.

`plan` runs the standard test's static checks without compiling, launching or creating the report. It lists the resolved launch plan, schedule, per-check elapsed time, failures and remedies. A stale build is reported; `test` rebuilds it automatically before launch. Native options and canonical profile inputs are checked; preserve unexplained differences before resetting a managed slot. Runtime-only checks still run in the client.

`check` accepts the same candidate arguments and exercises activation, available source/work checks, short captures and restoration without the two-minute conditioning period. It reports no performance or visual qualification. Use it when checking whether a newly integrated candidate runs; use `test` for a development performance comparison. Frozen Bliss qualification cannot use `check`.

`test` uses the fixed native/candidate/native-return protocol described below. `report` reads existing reports without launching anything, including historical reports. Its decision gives drift comparison precedence over an averaged positive mean, and identifies invalid runs or recovery requirements. It does not grant optimization closure or compatibility qualification. Phase timings in `summary.json` include nested profile preparation/restoration details; do not sum nested details into the total again.

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

The command automatically selects the existing Linux ARM64 launcher on that platform. Explicit `linux_arm64_runtime.py` commands remain supported. It finds an installed full JDK21 or a cached Gradle JDK21; an explicit JAVA_HOME retains precedence. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

## Acceptance and analysis

Analysis uses independent JVM runs as replicates, not correlated individual
frames. Report each run's GPU elapsed and total-frame wall median/p95, plus
`1000 × elapsed_seconds / render_frames`. Per-arm median/min/max/MAD and all six
paired block contrasts retain original→OFF, original→FULL, OFF→FULL,
original→ADAPTIVE, OFF→ADAPTIVE and FULL→ADAPTIVE separately.

The primary throughput ratio is original elapsed per rendered frame divided by
ADAPTIVE elapsed per rendered frame. 1.5 × means 50% greater throughput and
33.333% less elapsed time per frame. The repeated timing target requires all
32 valid runs; every original→ADAPTIVE block at least 1.5 ×; median at least
1.5 ×; every OFF→ADAPTIVE block faster; each original→ADAPTIVE GPU median
improved; GPU and total-frame p95 at most 1.05 × original in every block; and
relative run MAD ≤ 5% for each arm's GPU median, total-frame median and elapsed
per-frame mean. No single block, incomplete batch or nominal retention passes.
These are preregistered stability/target guards, not a confidence interval.

An acceptance **candidate** also requires separately accepted, exact-scope
consuming-stage driver/layout/cache/sampler/fallback evidence and representative
still/motion quality evidence. The script never manufactures these approvals.
Final screenshot headers/hashes prove capture extent and provenance, not motion
quality. Preserve adverse/contaminated windows; stop on observed quality loss or
input/runtime drift. Do not replace runs within a frozen batch to chase a gain.

```text
yaw = degrees(atan2(-S.x, S.z)); pitch = degrees(asin(S.y))
```

# Cost-map stage 1 implementation

2026-11-08. Implements only [COST_MAP section 11 stage 1](COST_MAP.md#11-delivery-sequence-and-acceptance).
No Minecraft client, GPU workload, benchmark, live capture or machine qualification.

`src/devClient/java/com/pp/shaderlod/dev/timing/costmap/` contains:

- `CostMapRecords`: schema version 1, immutable capture/cohort, DH identity, frame,
  scope/invocation, CPU/GPU event, coverage/health and aggregate records. Capture
  metadata has required typed keys; unavailable values require an explicit fact
  and evidence/reason. DH settings retain exact keys with evidence, alongside typed
  artifact/loader/compatibility/distance/residency identity. Scope feature links
  are metadata only, not attribution or an implemented catalog. No aggregate is
  computed here. Raw durations stay integer nanoseconds. Unknown counts and
  unavailable thread CPU remain null. A measured zero is valid; structural absence
  uses a status/reason with null duration, including absent DH `NOT_APPLICABLE`.
- `ScopeRegistry`: one owner, stable positive integer IDs keyed by graph, stage,
  program, operation and discriminator, with names solely for display. Re-registering
  the same key is idempotent only with identical metadata. Each invocation gets a
  capture/cohort/window/epoch/frame/graph identity, event and parent IDs, execution
  ordinal, thread/context and independent DH stage/world-shadow/opacity context.
  Invocation `observed` describes execution evidence; entry outcomes describe
  measurement results. Every entry has separate explicit CPU/GPU outcomes; a
  missing payload is `UNKNOWN` for that dimension, never implicit zero. Observations
  join by event and dimension; a CPU-only record does not overwrite a GPU result.
  `endMissing` retains an executed but unmeasured invocation;
  `missing` records explicit per-scope absence/eligibility reasons. At boundaries,
  unclassified registered scopes in that graph get `UNKNOWN`, never implicit zero
  or inferred nonexecution. Counts without observation remain null.
- `CounterDelta`: pure unsigned nanosecond-counter decoding, including one bounded
  modular wrap. The caller must independently establish a maximum interval below
  the modulus and change clock generation on reset/disjoint. Raw ticks alone cannot
  distinguish wrap, reset or multiple wraps. No GL query is issued or retrieved.

Limits independently bound registered scopes (including old graphs), active depth,
pending results and combined buffered entries/coverage. Overflow throws
`CapacityException`, stops the collector permanently, retains buffered evidence and
exposes loss/reason through out-of-band health even when no event slot remains.
No eviction or automatic restart occurs. A drain removes only completed buffered
entries; it never resets IDs, loss counters or pending ownership. Consumers must
retain the scope dictionary and health with every batch. Pending/open identities
remain bounded and their health counts remain visible after a capacity stop;
they are incomplete, not measured zero. Rejected records count as lost events;
byte sizes, query-pool limits and live timer diagnostics are null until observed.

Boundary changes invalidate open CPU scopes with a reason. Frame counter restart
requires a greater epoch; graph generations cannot regress and old scope IDs cannot
be used in the new graph. GPU pending and terminal records are append-only state
transitions joined by invocation/event ID, not independent samples to sum. Late
results retain original issue identity plus separate retrieval identity. Close

`TuningWindow.InputPause` stores only the first observed pause timestamp.

pause branches return, so the subtraction cannot be assigned to a readiness
request created halfway through the same pause.

The pose8second and mesh12second checks remain before poseReady and

reset active deadlines or accept a late ready state first. Motion resets/requests

intentional route restart and does not double-credit a fresh pose timestamp.

operations still establish their own clocks; this fix does not change those
request boundaries. Source/options/scene/video/restoration guards, sampling

# Benchmark guide

For optimization iteration use the maintained standard test, on the authorized machine with a prepared managed client slot and authentic original pack and options:

```sh
python3 scripts/run_benchmark.py test \
  --profile /path/to/prepared/client \
  --pack /path/to/original-pack.zip \
  --pack-options /path/to/original-pack.zip.txt \
  --feature PUBLIC_OPTIMIZATION_ID \
  --output /path/to/fresh/report
```

On Linux ARM64 use `python3 scripts/linux_arm64_runtime.py benchmark test` with the same arguments. Select an existing loader/version/scene slot; keep the report outside that slot and on the same filesystem as the profile. Confirm the lane is free and the inputs match the intended tuple before launch. Do not reset a slot owned by a client or interrupted operation. `python3 scripts/run_storage.py checkout --help` describes managed checkout. Use `run_storage.copytree` for profile/world copies; it enforces storage limits.

The standard test targets the prepared NeoForge 1.21.1 benchmark protocol. It renders native Off for 120 seconds before measurement, then acquires native Off, singleton candidate through normal Apply, then native Off return: 20 seconds each, with separate warmup, startup and recovery within a 900-second budget. Conditioning was added after repeated first-to-return drift; it does not prove stability. It records total-frame timing, drift, stills and restoration in the report. A valid slower result is still a result; a failed or invalid run is not a speed conclusion. Inspect `summary.json`, errors and restoration before proceeding. A short result is not proof of visual equivalence, DH/PBR compatibility or final closure. Compare matched total-frame measurements and disclose drift and scope.

G01 MakeUp copy elimination and G02 BSL mip elimination also collect existing untimed work witnesses after each measurement, disarming them before further timing. The BSL witness requires a separate untimed reload; inspect its completeness rather than inferring execution from parsed directives. G04 MakeUp `translucent_fastpath` requires `--saved-pose 9`: the maintained caller places one honey block in the backed-up save before all arms to cover the non-water/glass translucent class. Client visibility is checked; whole-save restoration removes the fixture after shutdown, including failed runs. Use `--width` and `--height` for the actual fullscreen mode (currently 2560×1600 on the local Asahi display).

The standard test records the prepared profile’s resource-pack file identities and freezes its selection requests. It requires those requests to be loaded before conditioning and checks the same actual selection before every arm; silent incompatible-pack removal refuses timing. Selection is enforced at those boundaries; resource bytes are not continuously rehashed. Saved pose11 is a close view of the existing stone gallery for native PBR material coverage.

For the new CPU qualification work, `--features quad_command_compaction,shadow_admission_cache` (optionally adding `index_scalar_cache`) tests only those CPU requests on the pinned original archive, retaining the exact complete native option map. Compaction requires the admission cache. The test requires actual returned compaction batches, scalar hits when requested, and admission-cache progress captured at the timing boundaries before later status queries. Command-entry counts are not GL draw counts; execution without fewer entries remains a valid outcome. Normal master Off/On Apply may reload the native pipeline; record that transition and require stable pipeline/terrain-program identities within each timing interval. Setup reload cost is reported separately, so steady-state timing does not establish amortized net benefit. Current CPU subset tests do not admit DH.

`--scene natural-terrain` selects the existing prepared `ShaderLOD-Smoke` world at its native spawn, seed8675309, with the same CPU-subset and no-DH constraints. The scene has a separate explicit diagnostic launch flag; it enables no occlusion-query mode, performs no cave scan and constructs no geometry. Saved-pose overrides are refused. Whole-save capacity-checked backup and canonical profile restoration remain mandatory. Record the actual spawn/camera and distinguish total-frame results from whole-render CPU intervals.

Cross-family public `early_alpha` tests for Sildur, Solas and AstraLex now require the matching family's actual owned CUTOUT/source-ready state before candidate timing and qualified permission progress around the window. Native controls must show no permission progress. Counts are cumulative runtime admissions and bracketing intervals, not avoided fragments or saved texture queries. Keep native materials/AA and actual sampler guards intact; refusal is not an optimization speed result.

`--untimed-diagnostic retained-copies` adds a read-only copy inventory after each standard public arm, including CPU subsets. It checks pinned API, stable metadata and returned copy submissions per physical target, then disarms before timing. It does not establish GPU completion, unused history or permission to delete an attachment or copy. Join its targets to current and next-frame reads/writes before proposing removal.

G03 MakeUp early-alpha captures existing qualified-draw counters in snapshots and its untimed source/admission diagnostic after each arm. The permission-based route requires an admitted context beforehand and qualified-counter progress afterward; these are admission counts, not avoided fragments. The Asahi post-sample route has no draw permission: it instead requires the typed rewrite receipt and all current source/input checks. Its timing remains explicitly source-setup-only evidence, without linked consumption or fragment coverage proof. CPU-cost profiling remains disabled for ordinary plans.

BSL reflection and AO sample-reuse tests retain untimed draw-admission status; admission is not a saved-query count. Photon is validated by its separate pinned live-pixel-budget producer and manifest. Its generated solid-terrain program marker is checked at its exact declared value; unknown added options and changes to original native options still fail.

The standard test also accepts `--candidate c01-bounds` without `--feature` for the existing finite private extra-occlusion prototype. It requires the exact original MakeUp9.5g/native100 map and no DH. Both controls and the candidate retain master Off with empty public requests; only the private current-frame query mode changes (prefix1, groups32). Actual query/read progress is required before and after candidate timing. This is separate from public depth priming.

Use `--candidate g10-exact-bloom` without `--feature` for the finite private MakeUp exact zero-dither bloom reuse variant. It preserves native100 and four original additions, and requires an actual pre-detach compile/link receipt joined to consuming bloom draws. The original pack is used for both Off controls. Staged private packs and sidecars are backed up/restored by the operation; diagnostic reloads acknowledge rendered readiness and settled configuration. An integer work image runs after all three timed arms, with its actual writer texture joined to readback. Source-expression opportunity counts are not hardware-fetch savings. `--candidate g10-native-control` uses the same private producer with selector0 and requires native linked source; it is explicitly labeled a known-null control, with descriptive timing retained and no optimization conclusion.

The experimental combination command accepts `--features dead_frame_copy,early_alpha,translucent_fastpath,ao_attenuation` instead of `--feature`, with any supported subset of two to four MakeUp G01/G03/G04/G06 features. It enables explicit benchmark-only admission and preserves the native100/API/platform/source checks. Every requested compile control must be active. G01 requires complete executed-copy witnesses (6/3/6 per completed final pass), including candidate coverage before timing; G04 and G06 require matching selected-source markers. G03 retains its complete native CUTOUT fragment pin and obtains untimed shader-object/link/submission evidence; submitted batches are not avoided-fragment counts. Witnesses disarm in `finally`, and timing refuses an armed G03 observer. Ordinary clients retain their prior route restrictions. This measures tested subsets; it does not establish an exhaustive optimum or an all-twelve-active configuration.

`--scene translucent-fixture --saved-pose 9` uses the maintained honey-block fixture for every arm, including subsets without G04. G04 uses that fixture by default. `--scene saved` explicitly retains the unmodified authored saved scene, allowing coverage and performance scenes to be considered separately; record its saved pose and do not infer G04 branch coverage from the request flag. Whole-save/profile restoration remains mandatory.

`--with-g10` adds the private exact zero-dither G10 kernel to an explicit supported combination. `--g10-control` uses the same observer setup with the kernel disabled. Both collect completed draws in explicit untimed intervals and refuse timing if the observer remains armed. The pre/post draw counters describe those untimed intervals, not timed work. A qualified constructor gate is separate from native options; approximate pairing is never enabled. The observer must join actual compiled shader objects, successful link and consuming draws at the actual bloom stage (composite2 when G01 moves it). Missing link/source/progress evidence refuses timing. `--candidate c01-bounds --features ...` similarly tests the finite private C01 addition with generated-source/native100 verification, unchanged attached native SOLID hashes and existing query/depth/raster checks. These additions are development experiments; original-only C01/G10 commands remain available. Physical fetch savings, motion/pixel equivalence and broad DH/PBR compatibility require separate evidence.

`--candidate g08-native-bound --saved-pose 7` tests the private original-derived MakeUp native100 single-layer cloud bound. `--g08-bound-layout split` keeps the native prefix in a separate loop; `alu` instead retains every native texture query and guards only nonpositive-density opacity calculations, without an atlas. Before conditioning, an untimed work archive verifies the consuming cloud texture and atlas bytes, effective sampling, native opacity at omitted positions and native numeric RGB across sixteen Iris frame-counter residues. The lean candidate uses the same sampling proof, disarmed before timing; the ALU mode proves only the native cloud image. Both controls and the candidate keep public requests empty and master Off; staged archives and sidecars remain operation-owned. The work archive displays native RGB. These finite checks and source-expression counts do not establish motion, whole-image equivalence, physical fetch savings or public/default qualification.

`--untimed-diagnostic g02-family` captures actual linked selected sources, pass sampler/writer bindings, mip-generation returns and two completed frames plus the next reset for the existing singleton mip candidate. The observation disarms before timing and releases its records after export. Executed omission is separate from source liveness and image equivalence. Photon can use `--scene nether` for its pinned non-Overworld route. `--candidate g02-native-mips --g02-public-contrast` adds a descriptive fourth public-integration arm between the private deletion and native return; it keeps the existing non-PBR profile and normal Apply for the public arm. The private deletion also accepts the separately pinned native advanced-material profile without widening public admission.

`--candidate g02-photon-native --untimed-diagnostic g02-family --scene nether` tests the private original-derived Photon native366/no-DH cloud-pass and RT11 mip deletion. Both controls and the candidate keep master Off and public requests empty. Exactly two Nether cloud passes are disabled; Overworld/End and the earlier live RT5 mip are retained. The observer requires matching remaining pass order/mip sets, no active 9–12 sampler reads and exactly two omitted cloud draws. Attached source equality and liveness remain separate recorded analysis; this does not grant public/default or broad quality/compatibility qualification.

The new private original-derived commands `--candidate n04-bliss-sky`, `--candidate n04-bliss-zero`, `--candidate n02-bliss-unused-rt12` and `--candidate n03-bliss-fog-copy` require exact Bliss native463, Overworld and no DH/Voxy. Use the original archive and native option sidecar, no public feature requests. Each owns an untimed two-frame linked-source/physical-graph observation, disarmed before timing. The sky candidate bypasses only the immediately overwritten sky SSAO result. Its depth census retains the source receipts, waits for settled rendering and rearms without reloading. It joins the actual Iris depth owner, equal pre/post-consumer census and second observed frame's final screenshot. Observation ordinals and actual Iris frame numbers remain separate. These are potential input texels, not executed branches. The zero candidate guards only the active opaque emission function and retains the native fallback; the native translucent emission call is inactive. RT12 removes only the two unused attachment entries and corresponding depth store. The fog-copy candidate preserves all shader bytes and removes only the reviewed final RT13 copy at 2560×1600. These are private prototypes, not public Apply/Off/Cancel or DH/PBR qualification.

For native CPU standard comparisons on Linux without DH, optional `--cpu-placement` records read-only `sched_getcpu` samples at each renderer boundary and prelaunch CPU cluster topology. The default is off. Boundary histograms do not measure residence, per-core CPU time or causation; migration that returns to the same CPU is invisible and observer overhead is uncalibrated. The observer does not change affinity or governors. Keep the usual command/cache-work, graph identity, exact native options and restoration requirements.

Optional `--render-cpu 4 --cpu-placement` declares a controlled Linux CPU diagnostic for those same CPU comparisons. It pins only the calling render thread during each settled timed capture and verifies the original CPU mask is restored before the next reload or observation. Existing threads retain their masks; a detected surviving new thread inheriting the temporary restricted mask invalidates the run and the owned client stops. This endpoint census does not detect transient children that exited before the final scan. Every recorded head/tail boundary must match the declared CPU, without unknown samples or migration. The default is disabled. No governor or global settings change is made. This diagnoses cluster scheduling effects; it does not qualify ordinary scheduling, fixed CPU frequency or general performance.

Private `--candidate n04-solas-lean-alpha` requires exact original Solas V3.7b/native428, Overworld without DH/Voxy and empty public requests. Only terrain fragment includes redirect to three private lighting clones; vertex and non-terrain files remain native. The post-floodfill alpha guard uses the actual Iris GREATER reference. Five downstream query expressions use explicit LOD zero only under current effective nonmip sampler proof. Permission zero preserves the original implicit queries and rejection. Settled linked-source comparison approves the complete shader delta before arming the exact current CUTOUT program/interface. Permission is rechecked after setup and revoked before setup/reset and during recovery. Counters establish setup grants, not completed draws or avoided fragments. This is a private benchmark prototype, not public or DH/PBR qualification.

Private `--candidate n04-sildur-underwater-ao` requires exact Sildur Vibrant 2.02 Extreme/native115 and Overworld without DH/Voxy, with empty public requests. Use underwater saved pose3. It moves only the native SSDO call inside its existing uniform condition; native AO remains one when that condition is false. Two settled returned deferred quads must report actual `isEyeInWater==1`. Whole attached-source comparison permits only this guard movement; native options, AA and other operations remain unchanged. Source call avoidance does not establish physical sample savings: the compiler may already eliminate the unused work. Native/candidate/return timing and restoration remain mandatory.

`--candidate n03-photon-cloud-copy --scene nether` requires exact original Photon native366 without DH/Voxy, with native AA/options retained. It appends only four terminal flip properties at composite16; all shader bytes, passes and mips remain native. Expected final-copy counts are 9/5/9, with only RT9–12 absent in candidate. Earlier physical bindings and retained copy order must match. These properties are unsafe for Overworld cloud history: the owned caller checks Nether synchronously before candidate reload, then checks activation and source/physical evidence. Restore the original before changing dimensions. Minecraft's final color image can have a different Iris framebuffer wrapper; ownership is joined by the actual shared texture, not framebuffer-number equality.

`--untimed-diagnostic cpu-admission-cost` requires the exact public CPU triple `--features quad_command_compaction,shadow_admission_cache,index_scalar_cache`, no DH, and a standard test. It observes at least128 completed frames after candidate timing, at the actual compaction/scalar consumer checks. Both clock aggregates include observer overhead; wall time is not pure GPU waiting. Clock reads are disarmed in scored windows, while ordinary plans disable the diagnostic branch. Own-JVM DH-permission transitions test cache invalidation and restore every property; without DH installed they do not qualify live-DH admission. No consumer permission is reused or safety guard removed.

If the harness or inputs fail, preserve the failure, restore/release owned resources, fix the maintained harness or inputs, and retry. Do not copy harness code into report-local callers, inject launcher overrides, relax admission after failure, or substitute custom scripts for the standard result. Diagnostics are diagnostic and do not replace it. One Linux ARM64 BSL standard run completed with verified restoration and independent review; this does not establish behavior for other configurations or future changes. See [experiment history](EXPERIMENTS.md).

Keep reports, worlds, downloads, builds and captures out of Git. Do not kill unrelated processes. If restoration refuses due to unknown changes, preserve the data and inspect ownership and recovery before acting.

Runtime dependencies and original shader-pack inputs are stored under `dependencies/`. Keep active experiment output in `dev/experiments/` and any retained evidence in `experiment-evidence/`; both are local and outside Git. Prepared clients and worlds remain under `run-workloads/`.
